said_voted.caption: Posts are shown as written. A post is matched to a vote only when it names the bill number or the bill's official title. A post can mention a bill for many reasons.
said_voted.topic_caption: Recent posts grouped by simple keyword rules that are identical for every member (published at /x_topic_rules.json). A post listed under a topic is not claimed to be about any specific vote; a post can appear under more than one topic.

I represent the busiest airport in the world, so I know how important it is to maintain safe, stable air travel. I also represent thousands of workers across our airports and airlines whose livelihoods depend on a well-functioning transportation system.

The tragic accidents, communication failures and close calls we have seen recently are absolutely unacceptable. Congress has already provided $14.4 billion in modernization funding for the FAA, but they have only spent $5 billion. We need to make sure they are putting that money to work! 

Our travelers and workers, whether they call the #FightingFifth home or are just passing through, deserve it.

My office has been in contact with Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport officials as we monitor the nationwide ground stop.

Travelers should check their flight status directly with their airline before heading to the airport and monitor @FAANews for updates. We will continue sharing information as it becomes available.

On November 13, 2018, I was led out of the Georgia Capitol, hands zip tied behind my back for demanding that every vote be counted for my friend and democracy warrior, Stacey Abrams. 

I now get to walk back through those doors with my head held high to work with our next governor, Keisha Lance Bottoms. Read more about the journey since that day in my latest op-ed in the AJC: https://t.co/QihmuTvhQS

No one should be criminalized for seeking or providing essential health care. Period.

Since Roe v. Wade was overturned, states have increasingly targeted patients, providers, and other third parties just for giving or getting the help they need. 

I am introducing this resolution because healthcare is not a crime, and medical decisions should not lead to targeting.

Essential healthcare like abortion, contraception, and gender-affirming care should be available to everyone without threat of persecution.

What better way to honor our veterans the day after Veterans Day than by passing the Major Richard Star Act, legislation that will finally give our combat-injured veterans the benefits they have earned.
 
I am always proud to fight for the veterans in the #FightingFifth and across the country who have fought so hard for us.

Today, we honor the veterans in the #FightingFifth and beyond who have served our country.

I am deeply grateful for the countless sacrifices you and your families have made. During Military Family Appreciation Month, we must also recognize the loved ones who make that service possible.

The best way I can thank our veterans for their service is to fight for them in D.C. and back home.

I will never stop fighting for those who have fought so hard for us.

Living with endometriosis since I was 14, I know firsthand the physical, financial, and systemic challenges that come with getting a diagnosis. For many patients, that diagnosis takes 7–10 years, often resulting in worsening pain and delays in care.

Expanding access to pelvic floor physical therapy and rehabilitation services can improve quality of life and reduce the long-term impact of delayed care.

That’s why my colleagues and I are calling on HHS to ensure pelvic floor rehabilitation receives equal coverage, whether needed after childbirth or because of endometriosis. Access to care should never depend on the reason someone needs it.

Thank you, Dolores, for showing generations of changemakers what it means to fight out loud and on purpose.

I’m sick and tired of the Trump Administration’s endless attacks on our right to vote.

Despite ample evidence that noncitizen voting is extremely rare, Trump continues to manufacture this criss while laying the groundwork and preemptively undermining election results.

I have seen this playbook before, and I refuse to stand by while our democracy is under attack across our country.

I am heartbroken by the senseless school shooting in Oregon that took the lives of three children and one teacher and left two others in critical condition.
 
This is the 36th shooting on K-12 school grounds across America this year. That is 36 too many.
 
The impact of this tragedy will be felt throughout the entire community for years to come.
 
We must take meaningful action to strengthen our gun laws and protect our children from the constant fear of being shot in their schools. Our children deserve to learn in safety, not fear. Thoughts and prayers alone are not enough. We need action.

Across the #FightingFifth today, people are wearing purple to stand in solidarity with survivors of domestic violence.

Intimate partner violence remains far too prevalent across our country, and too many people suffer in silence. We must continue raising awareness, standing with survivors, and ensuring no one feels alone. Know that support is available through the following resources:

💜 Partnership Against Domestic Violence: 404-873-1766
💜 Georgia Domestic Violence Hotline: 1-800-334-2836
💜 National Domestic Violence Hotline: 1-800-799-7233

158 days of gas above $4. A new record.
 
Since Trump’s reckless war in Iran began, the average American household has paid an extra $2,000 in costs.
 
You feel it at the pump, at the checkout line, and every time you sit down to try to make your monthly budget work. Working families in the #FightingFifth and beyond shouldn’t have to pay the price for this administration’s reckless decisions.

Voting rights are the foundation of every policy issue. If you care about healthcare, affordability, climate, or any other issue, you care about protecting our right to vote.

When the Trump administration attacks that right, they're attacking that very foundation. We will not be silenced, and I will always fight to make sure every voice in the #FightingFifth and across the country is heard.

That’s why I co-authored a letter urging HUD Secretary Turner to put the funds for the Whole-Home Repairs Act to work — funds we secured through the historic 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act.

Georgians in the #FightingFifth and beyond can have confidence in our elections and in your vote.

Nonviolence helped change the course of American history in the #FightingFifth and beyond.

Congressman John Lewis saw this firsthand. As a young activist, he helped lead a movement grounded in nonviolent action, and later, as a member of Congress, he introduced a resolution supporting National Nonviolence Week to raise awareness about youth violence.

Today, as youth violence continues to affect communities across the country, we must carry that legacy forward.

My resolution would establish this week as “National Nonviolence Week,” encouraging programs and activities aimed at raising awareness and preventing youth violence.

Breaking down barriers between young people and the ballot is exactly why I introduced the Youth Voting Rights Act — to make sure polling places are available on university campuses in the #FightingFifth and across the country.
 
The right to vote is under attack, and we have to do everything we can to make every voice heard, and that includes our college students.

Welcome to #SecureTheBallot — my new series about the fight for our right to vote and what it means to protect that right today.
 
We’re starting here in the heart of the #FightingFifth with my friend, mentor, and predecessor, the late, great Congressman John Lewis.
 
Because before we talk about casting your ballot, we need to remember the people who fought to make sure you had the right to cast it.

🚨 REMINDER: Today is the last day to register to vote!

If you haven't registered yet, don't wait. Get yourself registered today and make your plan to vote, y'all. 

Early voting: October 13-30th 
Election day: November 3rd

Visit https://t.co/ZrlLskuHme for more information. https://t.co/2wKBoFxrIr

Our Service Academies offer more than just an education; they provide teamwork, discipline, and perseverance-all virtues that help our #FightingFifth students succeed.

I truly enjoyed spending the afternoon with #FightingFifth students, celebrating them and cheering them on as they explore new opportunities.

The deadline for Service Academy nominations is November 2. Learn more here: https://t.co/fO29zg21Et

I represent the busiest airport in the world, so I know how important it is to maintain safe, stable air travel. I also represent thousands of workers across our airports and airlines whose livelihoods depend on a well-functioning transportation system.

The tragic accidents, communication failures and close calls we have seen recently are absolutely unacceptable. Congress has already provided $14.4 billion in modernization funding for the FAA, but they have only spent $5 billion. We need to make sure they are putting that money to work! 

Our travelers and workers, whether they call the #FightingFifth home or are just passing through, deserve it.

At #COP31 in Turkey I’m connecting with global leaders, exchanging ideas, and learning about solutions that advance both climate progress and economic opportunity.

And it’s a reminder that Atlanta is everywhere! I’ve already had the chance to connect with a Coca-Cola executive https://t.co/iIASijou6m

My office has been in contact with Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport officials as we monitor the nationwide ground stop.

Travelers should check their flight status directly with their airline before heading to the airport and monitor @FAANews for updates. We will continue sharing information as it becomes available.

What better way to honor our veterans the day after Veterans Day than by passing the Major Richard Star Act, legislation that will finally give our combat-injured veterans the benefits they have earned.
 
I am always proud to fight for the veterans in the #FightingFifth and across the country who have fought so hard for us.

roll_calls.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Housing for the 21st Century Act (H R 6644)
roll_calls.plain_language: This bill establishes and modifies various federal housing programs. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

roll_calls.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Concur in Senate Adt to House Adt to Senate Adt — Housing for the 21st Century Act (H R 6644)
roll_calls.plain_language: The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act establishes and modifies various federal housing programs. This vote, under suspension of the rules, was on accepting the Senate's latest changes to the bill after the chambers traded versions, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea accepts the Senate's version; a Nay opposes it.

post.text:
Nearly 7 million Americans live in homes that need significant repairs.
 
That’s why I co-authored a letter urging HUD Secretary Turner to put the funds for the Whole-Home Repairs Act to work — funds we secured through the historic 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act.
 
Because safe, healthy homes shouldn’t be a partisan issue. Families in the #FightingFifth and across the country deserve better.
